# Results — Study 147 (FX-Momentum) on real G10 FX tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: rank G10 currencies
each month by their trailing **12-1 month** log-return vs USD; go **long top-3, short
bottom-3** (equal weight within each leg), hold one month, rebalance monthly. The
benchmark is an identical portfolio with **random rankings** drawn i.i.d. each month,
averaged over 20 seeds. As-of **2026-06-14**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n months | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| Yahoo Finance G10 FX spot (9 pairs, daily) | 2006-05-31 to 2026-06-30 | 241 raw / **229 in-sample** | `b4c2f5d4f82a` |

Currencies (all expressed as foreign vs USD — positive = foreign ccy appreciated):
EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD, CAD, CHF, NZD, NOK, SEK. USD-base pairs (JPY, CAD, CHF, NOK, SEK)
are sign-inverted in the loader so all series have a uniform convention.

Yahoo Finance provides spot FX data from approximately 2003 for most pairs; after the
12-1 month warmup period the in-sample portfolio window begins May 2006.

## The honest test — 12-1 momentum vs random-ranking control (gross, cost = 0)

The random-ranking control is run over 20 independent seeds and averaged; this removes
the idiosyncratic noise of any single random draw and gives an honest baseline for zero.

| Arm | n months | Ann. mean | Ann. Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **12-1 momentum (long top-3, short bot-3)** | 229 | **-1.64%** | **-0.25** | **-1.17** |
| Random-ranking control (20-seed avg) | 229 | -0.28% | — | — |
| Momentum minus random | — | **-1.37%** | — | — |

- The momentum portfolio's gross annual return is **-1.64%**, HAC *t* = **-1.17** —
  **statistically indistinguishable from zero** (|t| < 2) and pointing in the wrong
  direction.
- It **does not beat the random control.** Averaged over 20 random seeds the random
  portfolio earns **-0.28%/yr**, outperforming the momentum portfolio by 1.37%/yr.
- The block-bootstrap 95% CI on the annualised Sharpe is **[-0.67, +0.16]** (89% of
  resamples negative).

## Could you trade it? — cost sweep (momentum portfolio, net)

At ~44% monthly turnover per leg (i.e., roughly 4-5 currency changes per month), costs
are a meaningful but not decisive headwind — the strategy is already negative gross:

| Cost (per leg, per month) | Net ann. mean | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | -1.64% | -1.17 |
| 2 bps | -1.75% | -1.24 |
| 5 bps | -1.90% | -1.36 |
| 10 bps | -2.17% | -1.54 |
| 20 bps | -2.70% | -1.92 |

At 5 bps/leg (institutional FX bid-offer) the net return is **-1.90%/yr** (t = -1.36).
At 10 bps/leg (a more conservative all-in estimate) it is **-2.17%/yr**. The strategy
has no positive break-even cost — it was never alive.

## Sub-period breakdown (gross) — the factor has decayed

| Period | n months | Ann. mean | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2006–2012 | 68 | -4.22% | -1.25 |
| 2013–2019 | 84 | -0.70% | -0.34 |
| 2020–2026 | 77 | -0.39% | -0.21 |

FX momentum — once a genuine academic factor from roughly 1976 to 2010 — has weakened
across all sub-periods in our sample. No sub-period shows |t| > 1.5. The trend from
the 2012 MSSMS paper is absent in post-publication data.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK** (borderline NONE). Gross HAC *t* = -1.17 (wrong sign), -1.64%/yr;
  the portfolio underperforms even a random-ranking control. There is no statistically
  real directional information in the 12-1 G10 FX momentum sort on Yahoo daily data
  from 2006 onward. The effect documented by Menkhoff et al. (2012) on 1976-2010 data
  used a richer universe (48 currencies) and appears to have decayed post-publication.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Gross edge is already negative; any realistic cost makes it
  a statistically meaningful loser. Monthly turnover ~44% per leg rules out any positive
  break-even cost structure for retail participants.
